summary: The latest visible arXiv announcement batch after the weekend contained a compact but high-quality set of papers around coherent vector-meson photoproduction in PbPb, small-x/EIC saturation observables after hadronization, relativistic hydrodynamic boundary conditions, DIS event-shape precision, and validation-centered physics AI/ML. The strongest selected papers emphasize experimentally or phenomenologically usable observables and likelihood- or simulation-facing validation rather than generic novelty claims.
strongest_paper: CMS observes a greater-than-5-sigma spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetry in coherent J/psi photoproduction in hadronic PbPb collisions, while the eHIJING saturation study and collider-inference validation paper are the strongest phenomenology and AI/ML-methodology entries.

papers.title: Spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetry of coherent J/psi photoproduction in hadronic PbPb collisions at sqrt(sNN) = 5.36 TeV
papers.abstract: CMS reports a measurement of the azimuthal asymmetry of muons from coherently photoproduced J/psi mesons with respect to the second-order event plane in hadronic PbPb collisions at 5.36 TeV. A negative A2 value is observed with significance above five standard deviations and is consistent with a model where the vector meson inherits photon linear polarization.

papers.title: Tracing Gluon Saturation through Hadronization at EIC
papers.short_authors: Weiyao Ke, Xu Liu, Yu Shi, Xin-Nian Wang, Jian Zhou
papers.abstract: The authors implement nonlinear small-x initial-state radiation in eHIJING and test how hadronization changes saturation signatures. Global hadronic recoil remains sensitive to underlying kT broadening while several conventional observables are strongly diluted.

papers.title: Thermal boundaries for relativistic fluids without a conserved charge
papers.short_authors: Lorenzo Gavassino, Soeren Schlichting, Gabriel S. Denicol
papers.abstract: A kinetic-theory slab model is used to derive boundary conditions for an ultrarelativistic fluid without conserved charge. The walls behave as modified absorbing boundaries rather than thermostats, and the initial-boundary-value problem is shown to be well posed.

papers.title: Hadronization effects and electroweak contributions in DIS one-jettiness
papers.short_authors: Radja Boughezal, Haotian Cao, Zhong-Bo Kang, Xiaohui Liu, Sonny Mantry, Frank Petriello
papers.abstract: The paper computes leading hadronization effects and massive electroweak-boson contributions for DIS 1-jettiness observables, including high-logarithmic-accuracy predictions and Pythia comparisons over HERA and EIC kinematics.

papers.title: A Differentiable Neural Surrogate for Photon Propagation in Neutrino Telescopes
papers.short_authors: Felix J. Yu, Berthy T. Feng, Nicholas Kamp, Carlos A. Arguelles
papers.abstract: A differentiable SIREN neural field learns the photon Green's function for IceCube and predicts sensor photon yields and arrival-time distributions. The surrogate is reported 50-100x faster than existing simulation with percent-level yield agreement and useful gradients.

papers.title: Reduced latent leakage does not reliably predict lower likelihood bias in collider inference
papers.abstract: A controlled collider-inference study finds that reducing nuisance readability in reusable embeddings does not reliably reduce profiled signal-strength bias. The result argues for likelihood-facing stress tests and held-out confirmation before claiming inference robustness.

papers.title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks for Jet Tagging on Quantum Hardware
papers.short_authors: Benjamin Jobilal, Jinghong Yang, Trevor Smith, Vincent Calvo, Zhong-Bo Kang, Shabnam Jabeen
papers.abstract: A permutation-invariant quantum graph neural network is applied to particle-cloud jet tagging tasks, including quark/gluon and up/down flavor tagging. The authors compare ideal simulations with PFN-like baselines and deploy scaled-down models on IBM and IonQ devices.

papers.title: FUSION: a skill-based research agent for publicly obtainable nuclear-physics codes
papers.abstract: FUSION packages code-specific agent skills for public nuclear-physics codes, with verified inputs, parsing, failure-mode notes, and benchmark reproduction before reporting results. It covers twenty codes spanning several nuclear-physics workflows, including heavy-ion transport.

papers.title: Chaos is Target-Blind in High-Energy QCD Evolution
papers.abstract: The paper argues that tangent-process statistics in fixed-coupling JIMWLK evolution can show chaos while being independent of the target ensemble under local color-isotropic noise assumptions. Nonlocal noise correlations evade the argument.

cautions.title: Spectator shadowing as the source of the breaking of NCQ scaling at RHIC-FXT and FAIR energies
cautions.abstract: The authors propose that spectator shadowing can explain the breaking of NCQ elliptic-flow scaling at low heavy-ion energies using a toy coalescence source and ballistic Glauber spectator model.
